claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you a few questions.

First, do you have any children you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I have a daughter, Alex. She's 4 years old and lives with me here in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you have a daughter named Alex who is 4 years old and lives with you in the UK.

To continue assessing your eligibility, do you currently live in the UK yourself?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

Next question: Are you responsible for Alex's care and upkeep - meaning you're the one looking after her day-to-day needs like food, clothes, and accommodation?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I look after her every day - her food, clothes, everything she needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment.

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, that's very helpful. One final question to complete my assessment:

Are there any special circumstances that apply to Alex's situation, such as:
- Is she in hospital or care?
- Does she live away from you for any periods?
- Or any other unusual circumstances I should be aware of?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, she was in care for a short period - just about a month - but she's back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that. To make sure I assess this correctly, I need to understand the timing:

When did Alex return home from care - how long ago did she come back to live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She came back fairly recently - it's only been a few weeks since she's been home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided, you meet all the criteria for Child Benefit:

✓ **Alex is under 16** - She's 4 years old, so well within the age requirement
✓ **You live in the UK** - You confirmed you're living in the UK
✓ **Alex lives with you** - She's currently living with you at home
✓ **You're responsible for her care** - You provide for all her day-to-day needs including food, clothes, and everything else
✓ **No one else is claiming** - Nobody else is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Regarding the period when Alex was in care (approximately one month), since she's now back home with you and you're providing her full care, this doesn't affect your eligibility. The rules allow for Child Benefit to continue for 8 weeks when a child is in care, and Alex was in care for less than that before returning to you.

**Next steps:** If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you can apply now. If you were previously claiming and stopped during the care period, you may need to update your circumstances with HMRC.

Please note: If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge, though you can still claim the benefit.
